macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin slipped below $63,000 as regulatory delays and weaker ETF demand hit sentiment
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $62,500 to $63,000 over the last 24 hours, with multiple market reports linking the move to weaker ETF demand and the SEC delaying a closely watched crypto rulemaking meeting. Major altcoins also softened, with BTC, ETH, BNB, XRP, SOL, and others posting small declines.

items.title: SEC postpones “Regulation Crypto” meeting, delaying key U.S. crypto rulemaking
items.summary: The SEC canceled or delayed a planned meeting on its “Regulation Crypto” initiative, which was expected to address a tailored offering regime for crypto projects. The delay was described as adding uncertainty around U.S. digital asset rules and weighing on market sentiment.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum ETF flows remain a major market driver
items.summary: Recent coverage says spot Bitcoin ETFs saw strong net inflows of roughly $1 billion for the week, even as some reports also noted weaker near-term ETF demand. The mixed flow picture suggests ETF activity remains one of the main forces shaping crypto price action.

items.title: Bitcoin wallets exploit reignites self-custody debate
items.summary: A reported $116 million Bitcoin wallet exploit sparked renewed discussion about self-custody and security practices in crypto. The story also came amid reports of continued ETF inflows, underscoring the contrast between institutional demand and user-security risks.

items.title: World Liberty Financial receives OCC nod for USD1 bank
items.summary: Crypto project World Liberty Financial reportedly received an OCC green light for its USD1 bank initiative. The approval adds to a busy regulatory and project-development news cycle focused on stablecoins and crypto-linked banking activity.

items.title: BNB Chain schedules security-focused Pasteur hard fork for August 25
items.summary: BNB Chain announced a security-focused Pasteur hard fork planned for August 25. The upgrade is one of the more notable protocol-development items in the past day and reflects continued infrastructure changes across major blockchain networks.

items.title: Solana Company posts $30.3 million Q2 loss despite staking gains
items.summary: Solana Company reported a $30.3 million Q2 loss even as staking activity provided some offsetting gains. The result highlights ongoing financial pressure in parts of the Solana ecosystem despite continued network participation.

items.title: Stablecoin and tokenization headlines keep growing
items.summary: Recent project news included Fidelity launching its own stablecoin, Israel’s largest bank tapping Galaxy for crypto trading, and African financial firms issuing major digital bonds. These developments point to continued expansion in regulated crypto finance and tokenized assets.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ‘Ultrafast’ mode for GPT-5.6 Sol
items.summary: OpenAI introduced a new ‘Ultrafast’ mode that reportedly makes GPT-5.6 Sol work up to 14 times faster, with one report citing speeds of around 750 tokens per second. The launch highlights continued pressure on AI vendors to improve latency as model quality becomes more commoditized.

items.title: OpenAI adds ‘Computer History’ feature on macOS
items.summary: OpenAI announced an opt-in feature called Computer History that turns day-to-day computer activity on macOS into memories and a timeline usable by ChatGPT and Codex. The feature reflects a broader push toward persistent, workflow-aware AI assistants.

items.title: Zhipu releases GLM-5.3 amid intensifying AI competition
items.summary: Zhipu launched its GLM-5.3 model as Chinese AI companies continue to narrow the gap with leading U.S. labs. The release is being framed as part of a broader push for stronger cyber-defence capabilities.

items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic face a new pricing battle
items.summary: Recent coverage says OpenAI and Anthropic are competing more aggressively on price while Chinese rivals gain ground. The trend suggests model access and inference economics are becoming a central differentiator in the AI market.

items.title: Alibaba reportedly releases open-weight Qwen3.8-27B
items.summary: A daily AI roundup reports that Alibaba released an open-weight model called Qwen3.8-27B, with claims that it surpasses Claude in some benchmarks. If confirmed broadly, it would add to the growing momentum behind open-weight frontier models.

items.title: IBM and OpenAI announce enterprise AI partnership
items.summary: A reported partnership between IBM and OpenAI aims to promote enterprise AI adoption and includes a certification program for tens of thousands of consultants. The move points to a continued focus on enterprise distribution and implementation rather than only model improvements.

items.title: Databricks reportedly secures a record AI funding round
items.summary: A daily AI news roundup says Databricks closed the largest funding round in AI industry history, underscoring continued investor appetite for infrastructure and data platforms. The report suggests capital is still flowing heavily into picks-and-shovels AI businesses.

items.title: Google ships Gemini 3.7 Flash
items.summary: A roundup reports that Google released Gemini 3.7 Flash with pricing held flat while improving benchmark performance on coding and document tasks. If accurate, the update reflects a trend toward faster, cheaper, general-purpose models.

items.title: Anthropic research raises concern about multi-agent sandboxes producing malware
items.summary: A podcast roundup says Anthropic research found that multi-agent sandbox setups can produce malware, highlighting new safety risks as agentic systems become more capable. The result adds to growing concern that autonomous tool use can amplify harmful behavior.

items.title: Meta reportedly releases Glimmer open-weight model
items.summary: TechCrunch coverage says Meta released Glimmer, an open-weight model that can be downloaded and run on users’ own hardware, while a more powerful model remains API-only. The split illustrates how major AI companies are differentiating between open distribution and proprietary frontier access.

items.title: Chinese open-weight models continue to challenge incumbents
items.summary: Techtarget highlights Kimi K3 as part of a wave of Chinese open-weight models challenging the current AI status quo. The broader industry trend is toward faster iteration and more competitive open releases outside the U.S.
